Trisha 解释道，英伟达的先进芯片是“美国减缓对手人工智能能力的关键”。但这种优势也是“单点故障”，因为美国的出口管制力度取决于少数公司及其内部人员的安全措施。
格雷厄姆认为，这一事件并不是美国情报部门的失败，“而是美国政府在管理国家安全威胁方面协调和政策执行方面的更广泛的失败”。由于人工智能行业容易受到知识产权盗窃和直接攻击，华盛顿在风险管理和出口政策执行方面“措手不及”。
“对于投资者来说，将英伟达的成功与黄仁勋分开是很困难的，而对于华盛顿来说，将英伟达与国家安全分开也几乎同样困难，”杰西说。她现在认为国会有机会对该公司对国家安全的影响进行更大的监督，并加强半导体出口管制。肯顿指出，国会对芯片限制的势头不断增强，例如《人工智能监督法案》、《芯片安全法案》和《匹配法案》。
展望未来，特丽莎敦促政府加强审查。她认为，“鉴于支持美国人工智能领先地位的公司很少，政策制定者应该认真考虑政府的直接监督”，例如对公司领导层及其主要客户的安全许可要求，以及对出口实体的安全审计作为出口许可证的先决条件。
由于英伟达股价下跌，今天市场小幅下跌。黄仁勋的离开让投资者怀疑，如果没有这位已成为其成功代名词的领导者，英伟达能否维持其主导地位。杰西推测，公司“将在一段时间内不稳定”。
这些股份比英伟达的股价还要高。格雷厄姆警告说，美国经济已经高度依赖于少数人工智能公司的命运，这些公司“也恰好是该国在地缘政治竞争的决定性领域中的主要战略资产”。其中一个失败可能会影响整个美国经济和国家安全生态系统。
除了销售芯片之外，英伟达还成为人工智能热潮的主要融资者——被称为“人工智能中央银行”——投资初创企业并为购买其产品的客户提供支持。杰西表示，未来几个月将展示“英伟达对人工智能需求本身的整合程度如何”。

What Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit means for Washington, Wall Street, and Beijing
It’s a lot to process. On Thursday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. But the implications extend beyond the man and his former company, a critical engine of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom because of its leading-edge computer processors. Below, Atlantic Council experts work through how the personnel shakeup could impact US policy, global markets, and more.
TODAY’S EXPERT REACTION BROUGHT TO YOU BY
Trisha Ray: Associate director and resident fellow at the GeoTech Center
Graham Brookie (@GrahamBrookie): Vice president for technology programs and strategy
Jessie Yin: Associate director with the GeoEconomics Center
Kenton Thibaut (@kentonthibaut): Senior resident China fellow at the Digital Forensic Research Lab
Nvidia’s advanced chips are “the linchpin of the United States’ leverage in slowing down the AI capabilities of its adversaries,” Trisha explains. But that advantage is also “a single point of failure,” since US export controls are only as strong as the security practices of a handful of companies and people within them.
Graham sees the incident not as a failure in US intelligence, “but rather a broader failure of coordination and policy execution in how the US government manages national security threats.” With the AI industry vulnerable to intellectual property theft and direct targeting, Washington was “caught flat footed” in risk management and export policy enforcement.
“As difficult as it is for investors to separate Nvidia’s success from Jensen Huang, it has become nearly as difficult for Washington to separate Nvidia from national security,” Jessie argues. She now sees an opening for Congress to exert greater oversight of the company’s impact on national security and tighten semiconductor export controls. Kenton points to growing momentum in Congress behind chip restrictions such as the AI Overwatch Act, the Chip Security Act, and the MATCH Act.
Going forward, Trisha urges greater government scrutiny. “Given how few companies underpin the US AI lead, policymakers should seriously consider direct government oversight,” she argues, such as security clearance–like requirements for company leadership and their major customers, as well as security audits of the exporting entities as a precondition for export licenses.
Markets were down slightly today, as Nvidia shares took a hit. Huang’s departure has investors wondering if Nvidia can sustain its dominance without the leader who became a synonym to its success. The company is “going to be unsteady for a while,” Jessie surmises.
The stakes are higher than Nvidia’s stock price alone. The US economy is already highly exposed to the fortunes of a handful of AI companies that “also happen to be the country’s primary strategic assets in a determinative domain of geopolitical competition,” Graham warns. A failure at one could reverberate across the US economy and national security ecosystem.
Beyond selling chips, Nvidia has become a major financier of the AI boom—known as “the central bank of AI”—investing in startups and supporting customers that buy its products. Jessie says that the coming months will show “how integral Nvidia has become to AI demand itself.”

Ahead of a planned meeting next week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Beijing warned Washington earlier today against further technology restrictions, Kenton notes.
Huang had long opposed strict export controls and was able to speak with both Trump and Xi. “But with Huang out of the picture, there is potentially more political leeway to push forward on a more hawkish approach,” Kenton says.
Jessie adds that the scandal has “permanently damaged the company’s credibility to push back on export controls,” relationships aside.
But tougher controls could invite retaliation, Kenton warns. “Beijing could answer new restrictions with curbs on critical minerals or probes of other American firms,” potentially complicating the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting.

（图片来源：SpaceX） Falcon 9 是一款两级、70 m 高、部分可重复使用的火箭，第一级使用九个 Merlin 1D 海平面发动机，第二级使用单个真空优化的 Merlin 1D。Falcon 9 的第一级着陆在自主无人机船上或着陆点，其整流罩在飞行后回收并重复使用。两个阶段都使用液体煤油和液氧作为推进剂。助推器 B1103 将在其第七次飞行中支持这项任务。此前，该助推器已支持 NROL-179、第一批传输层 A 和 E 以及三个星链任务的发射。猎鹰 9 号将搭乘 SpaceX 的无人机“当然我仍然爱你”着陆。米尔 |演示飞行 11 月 10 日星期二，韩国计划发射韩国军方小型卫星运载火箭和平号的第二次飞行。继 2023 年 12 月进行了不包括第二级的试飞之后，此次发射将是全尺寸火箭的首次轨道飞行。启动窗口于 05:00 UTC 开始，并延长至 09:00 UTC。和平号是一款四级固体燃料运载火箭，第四级采用液体燃料，可实现精确入轨。 2023 年 12 月飞行的版本能够运载 700 公斤至近地轨道，该版本疑似能够运载 1,000 公斤左右。长征2D |有效载荷未知 11 月 11 日星期三，长征 2D (CZ-2D) 火箭计划从酒泉卫星发射中心发射升空。
目前，发射计划于 11:40 UTC 进行，距离 11:32 UTC 开启并持续到 12:05 UTC 的窗口还有 8 分钟的时间。CZ-2D 将向轨道发射未知有效载荷。 CZ-2D 是一款两级、41 米高的运载火箭，能够向近地轨道 (LEO) 发射 3,500 公斤的重量。 CZ-2D的第一级和第二级均由四氧化二氮和不对称二甲肼提供动力，这两种推进剂都是自燃推进剂。周三的发射将是长征二号丁的第 107 次发射，也是 2026 年的第六次发射。快舟 11 |有效载荷未知本周第二个也是最后一个预定的中国任务

【原文 English Original】
Seven rockets from four countries are set to launch this week. Starship is set to attempt its most consequential mission yet, while Falcon 9 is set to launch a pair of classified payloads for the United States Space Force. The United Launch Alliance is scheduled to fly Vulcan on its return-to-flight mission, and Electron is set to reach a milestone 100th mission. Internationally, China and South Korea are set to launch an unknown payload and a demonstration mission, respectively. Falcon 9 | USSF-627 (“R-5”) The first launch of the week will feature Falcon 9 delivering a classified payload for the United States Space Force (USSF). The mission, designated USSF-627, was initially scheduled to launch on Sunday, Nov. 8. Falcon 9 is now set to take off from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB) on Monday, Nov. 9, at 7:07 PM PST (03:07 UTC on Nov. 10), four minutes into a window that extends until 11:03 PM PST (07:03 UTC on Nov. 10). Due to the classified nature of the payload, the exact quantity of satellites is unknown. Some indicators suggest a Starshield launch, based on drop zones for Falcon 9’s second stage. Starshield is a version of Starlink built for the United States government, with its primary customers being the USSF, National Reconnaissance Office, and the Space Development Agency. A Falcon 9 on the launch pad at Space Launch Complex-4E on Vandenberg Space Force Base. (Credit: SpaceX) Falcon 9 is a two-stage, 70 m-tall, partially reusable rocket that uses nine Merlin 1D sea-level engines on its first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Merlin 1D on its second stage. Falcon 9’s first stage lands either aboard an autonomous droneship or at a landing site, with its fairings being recovered and reused after flight. Both stages utilize liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen as propellants. Booster B1103 will be supporting this mission on its seventh flight. Previously, this booster has supported the launches of NROL-179, Tranche 1 Transport Layers A and E, and three Starlink missions. Falcon 9 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Mir | Demo Flight On Tuesday, Nov. 10, South Korea is set to launch the second flight of Mir, the South Korean military’s small satellite launch vehicle. This launch is set to be the first orbital flight of the full-scale rocket, following a test flight in December 2023 that did not include the second stage. The launch window opens at 05:00 UTC and extends until 09:00 UTC. Mir is a four-stage, solid-fuel launch vehicle with a liquid-fueled fourth stage for precise orbital insertion. The version that flew in December 2023 was capable of 700 kg to LEO, with this version suspected to be capable of around 1,000 kg. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload On Wednesday, Nov. 11, a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) rocket is scheduled to launch out of the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center. The launch is currently scheduled for 11:40 UTC, eight minutes into a window that opens at 11:32 UTC and extends until 12:05 UTC. CZ-2D will deliver an unknown payload into orbit. CZ-2D is a two-stage, 41 m-tall launch vehicle capable of delivering 3,500 kg to low-Earth orbit (LEO). CZ-2D’s first and second stages are both powered by dinitrogen tetroxide and unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine, both hypergolic propellants. Wednesday’s launch will be the 107th overall for CZ-2D, and sixth in 2026. Kuaizhou 11 | Unknown Payload The second and final scheduled Chinese mission of the week will see a Kuaizhou 11 rocket launch on Thursday, Nov. 12. Liftoff is set for 19:50 UTC from Site 95A at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, during a 45-minute launch window. Kuaizhou 11 is a four-stage Chinese rocket manufactured by the China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation. Standing 25.3 m tall, the rocket can loft 1,500 kg to LEO with a liftoff thrust of 1,250 kN. This mission will be the eighth overall Kuaizhou 11 mission and the fourth of 2026. Vulcan VC6L | Amazon Leo (LV-01) United Launch Alliance’s (ULA) Vulcan rocket is set to launch on Friday, Nov. 13, from Space Launch Complex 41 (SLC-41) at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The 30-minute launch window opens at 12:54 PM EST (17:54 UTC). This will be the first flight of Vulcan in over nine months, following the ejection of one of Vulcan’s GEM-63XL solid rocket boosters at T+69 seconds on the USSF-87 mission. Flying aboard Vulcan will be a stack of 40 Amazon Leo satellites for Amazon’s Leo satellite internet constellation, a rival to SpaceX’s Starlink. A ULA Vulcan (USSF-87) sits next to a SpaceX Crew Dragon (Crew-12). (Credit: Tyler Gray for NSF) Vulcan is a two-stage launch vehicle with a range of launch configurations. Vulcan’s first stage is powered by two BE-4 engines built by Blue Origin, running on liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. Its second stage, Centaur V, is powered by twin RL10C engines running on liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. Centaur V can be configured as Centaur LEO, High Energy, or Endurance. Vulcan can also be configured with solid rocket boosters to augment liftoff thrust, with options ranging from zero to two, four, or six boosters. The payload is encapsulated by either a short (15.5 m) or a long (21.3 m) fairing. Vulcan will debut the Vulcan VC6L variant, designated by six solid boosters and the long fairing option. Vulcan will debut the LEO-optimized Centaur V, which is 1.94 m smaller than the existing Centaur V High Energy, which has flown on all previous Vulcan launches. Additionally, this flight is a certification flight of this Vulcan configuration for the United States Space Force. Amazon Leo (LV-01) will be the first of 38 scheduled for Vulcan and the fifth overall mission for Vulcan. Starship | Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 Pending regulatory approval, Starship is set to fly its next, and most significant, mission no earlier than Friday, Nov. 13, at 4:45 PM CST (22:45 UTC). The launch window extends until 6:00 PM CST (00:00 UTC on Nov. 14). Flight 15 will feature two notable events: the first booster-catch attempt since Flight 8, following stage separation, and the first attempt to catch the ship, roughly 22 hours after liftoff. Starship is a two-stage, super-heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of lofting an estimated 100 tonnes. The first stage, named Super Heavy, features 33 Raptor 3 engines, running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen propellants. The second stage, named Starship, features six Raptor 3 engines, three sea-level and three vacuum-optimized, also running off of liquid methane and liquid oxygen. Flying on Flight 15 will be Ship 42 and Booster 22, both on their first flights. Flight 15 is expected to deliver 26 Starlink v3 satellites to LEO. Like Flight 14, three of these satellites will feature imaging capabilities for imaging the heat shield of Starship in orbit. Flight 15 will be the 15th full-stack launch of Starship and the fourth for the system’s V3 configuration. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (“R-6”) Falcon 9 is set to fly again on Friday, Nov. 13, from VSFB with another USSF mission. The designation for this flight is USSF-317. The launch window opens at 8:09 PM PST (04:09 UTC on Nov. 14), and lasts for four hours. This mission will fly another unknown quantity of presumed Starshield satellites to LEO. Booster B1100 will support this mission, marking its 11th flight. This booster has previously supported NROL-105, USSF-385, and eight Starlink missions. B1100 will land downrange aboard SpaceX’s droneship Of Course I Still Love You . Electron during its 95th launch “Happily Ever Faster.” Credit: Rocket Lab) Electron | The Mountain God Rises The last scheduled launch of the week will see Rocket Lab’s Electron launch from the Mahia Peninsula in New Zealand on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 05:30 UTC. This flight of Electron, named “The Mountain God Rises,” will deliver another iQPS satellite into LEO for iQPS’s synthetic aperture radar constellation (SAR). SAR is used to image the surface of the Earth and can penetrate through cloud layers. Electron is a two-stage small-lift vehicle capable of delivering up to 300 kg to LEO and 200 kg to Sun-synchronous orbit. The vehicle is fueled by liquid kerosene and liquid oxygen, which powers nine Rutherford engines on the first stage and a single vacuum-optimized Rutherford on the second stage. This mission will serve as Electron’s 100th overall mission — a notable milestone for the small rocket that first flew in 2017. In addition, this mission will serve as the 269th orbital launch attempt worldwide in 2026. ( Lead Image: Falcon 9 launches from Florida. Credit: Julia Bergeron for NSF) The post Launch Preview: Starship, Vulcan, and Electron launches scheduled for busy week appeared first on NASASpaceFlight.com .

双方周一宣布，日本首相高市早苗将于本周在马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟峰会期间与韩国总统李在明举行双边会谈。
高市宣布此次会谈是她计划在访问马尼拉参加东盟峰会以及在中国深圳参加亚太经济合作论坛期间举行的一系列会议的一部分。
韩联社援引韩国总统办公室发言人的话说，定于周二举行的会谈将重点讨论双边关系以及地区和国际安全问题。
预定举行的由首尔和东京的盟友美国、俄罗斯和中国参加的三边领导人峰会也可能被列入议程。
此次会议将是高市去年10月就任以来两国第四次双边峰会。
高市最后一次见到李是在五月，当时她前往韩国访问他的家乡安东。
这次访问是正在进行的“穿梭外交”或两国领导人互访的一部分，旨在加强邻国时而动荡的关系。近年来，这种关系变得更加牢固，两国领导人共同努力强调改善关系。
日本一直寻求逐步与韩国建立安全关系，两国定期与美国举行三边会议，会谈主要集中在拥有核武器的朝鲜。
高市还于一月份在她的家乡奈良会见了李在镕的会面，这次会面强调了两位领导人对巩固牢固的个人和双边关系的承诺。
高市和李明博都效仿他们的前任，搁置了多年来在历史问题上的争执，转而专注于“面向未来”的关系，并在全球动荡日益加剧的情况下宣扬邻国关系的“战略重要性”。

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will hold bilateral talks with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit in Manila this week, both sides announced Monday.
Takaichi announced the talks as part of a series of meetings she plans to hold during visits to Manila for the ASEAN summit and then in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.
The talks, scheduled for Tuesday, will focus on bilateral relations, as well as regional and international security issues, the Yonhap news agency quoted South Korea’s presidential office spokesperson as saying.
A scheduled trilateral leaders’ summit involving Seoul and Tokyo’s ally the United States together with Russia and China is also likely to be on the agenda.
The meeting will be their fourth bilateral summit since Takaichi took office in October last year.
Takaichi last met with Lee in May as she traveled to South Korea for a visit to his hometown of Andong.
That visit was a part of ongoing “shuttle diplomacy,” or mutual visits by the two countries’ leaders, intended to strengthen the neighbors’ at-times-tumultuous relationship. That relationship has grown stronger in recent years, and both leaders have made concerted efforts to emphasize improving ties.
Japan has sought to gradually build up security ties with South Korea, with the two countries regularly holding trilateral meetings with the U.S. — talks that have largely focused on nuclear-armed North Korea.
Takaichi also met Lee in January in her hometown of Nara for a meeting that highlighted the two leaders’ commitment to cementing strong personal and bilateral ties.
Both Takaichi and Lee have followed their predecessors in putting aside years of acrimony over historical issues, instead focusing on “future-oriented” ties and trumpeting the “strategic importance” of the neighbors’ relationship amid growing global turmoil.

content:
2026 年 11 月 13 日

日本横须贺——

由军事海运司令部运营的远征快速运输舰俾斯麦市号（EPF 9）迎来了新任指挥官，中校。蒂亚·迈尔斯在横须贺舰队活动船上举行的仪式上。迈尔斯从中校手中接过指挥权。 VanAnh McCormick，在将该船移交给 MILCREW II 之前担任军事船员 I 的指挥官。

“从我们的人员流动开始，我们不再是 MILCREW II 和 CIVMAR；我们都是俾斯麦市号航空母舰，”迈尔斯在向由水手和公务员组成的混合船员发表的讲话中说道。 “‘保持媒体报道’是我们的全部工作！我们必须在场并准备好参与，同时互相支持，以确保我们的成功。Crew I 奠定了基础，我们的工作就是在此基础上继续发展。Possumus Efficiemus：我们可以而且我们将会实现。”

迈尔斯是南卡罗来纳州哥伦比亚人，2014 年从弗朗西斯马里恩大学毕业并获得数学学士学位后，被任命为海军军官。她还拥有海军研究生院的高级工商管理硕士学位。

在海上，迈尔斯曾在阿利伯克号航空母舰 (DDG 51)、珍珠港号航空母舰 (LSD 52) 和哈珀斯渡口号航空母舰 (LSD 49) 上服役。
在岸上，她在圣地亚哥海军水面和水雷作战发展中心和水面高级作战学校担任两栖作战战术教官。迈尔斯接替了麦考密克，麦考密克于 2026 年 7 月接管了 MILCREW I 的指挥权，并带领船员完成了有史以来的首次 EPF 部署。部署期间，船员航行超过4000海里，访问了4个海外港口。机组人员为“锐剑”演习提供了后勤保障，并完成了任务要求的所有准备工作。此外，供应部门还入围了 David M. Cook 食品服务卓越奖的决赛。

俾斯麦号是EPF级第九艘舰艇。这些浅吃水、全铝制商用双体船旨在以 35 节的平均速度将 600 短吨军用货物运输 1,200 海里。该船设有用于直升机操作的飞行甲板、车辆卸载坡道部署以及增强沿海操作和港口通道的浅吃水。这些能力使 EPF 能够在严峻或受损的港口提供灵活的物流支持、快速运输和救灾。

该船的船员由军事人员和文职海员组成。 MILCREW 轮流部署，基地设在圣地亚哥，而该舰的母港是横须贺，由美国第七舰队负责作战控制。
军事海运司令部负责指挥和支持大约 140 艘民用船只的行动，这些船只为美国海军舰船补充海上补给、执行专门任务、在全球范围内预置战斗货物、提供支持服务以及向部署的美国部队运输军事装备和补给品。

【原文 English Original】
13 November 2026

YOKOSUKA, Japan --

The expeditionary fast transport USS City of Bismarck (EPF 9), operated by Military Sealift Command, welcomed its new commanding officer, Lt. Cmdr. Tia Myers, during a ceremony aboard the ship at Fleet Activities Yokosuka. Myers assumed command from Lt. Cmdr. VanAnh McCormick, who served as the Military Crew I commander before turning the ship over to MILCREW II.

“Starting with our turnover, we are no longer MILCREW II and CIVMARs; we are all USS City of Bismarck,” Myers said in her address to the hybrid crew of sailors and civil service mariners. “It is all of our job to ‘keep the press!’ We have to be present and ready to engage while supporting each other to ensure our success. Crew I laid the foundation, and it is our job to build upon it. Possumus Efficiemus: We can and we will accomplish.”

A native of Columbia, South Carolina, Myers commissioned as a naval officer in 2014 after graduating from Francis Marion University with a bachelor’s degree in mathematics. She also holds an executive master’s degree in business administration from the Naval Postgraduate School.

At sea, Myers served aboard USS Arleigh Burke (DDG 51), USS Pearl Harbor (LSD 52) and USS Harpers Ferry (LSD 49).

Ashore, she served as an amphibious warfare tactics instructor at the Naval Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center and Surface Advanced Warfighting School in San Diego. Myers relieved McCormick, who took command of MILCREW I in July 2026 and led the crew through its first ever EPF deployment. During the deployment, the crew sailed more than 4,000 nautical miles and visited four overseas ports. The crew provided logistics support for Exercise Keen Sword and completed all ready for tasking requirements. In addition, the supply department became a finalist for the David M. Cook Food Service Excellence Award.

Bismarck is the ninth ship in the EPF class. These shallow-draft, all-aluminum, commercial-based catamarans are designed to transport 600 short tons of military cargo 1,200 nautical miles at an average speed of 35 knots. The ship features a flight deck for helicopter operations, a vehicle offload ramp deployment, and a shallow draft that enhances littoral operations and port access. These capabilities allow the EPF to deliver flexible logistics support, rapid transport and disaster relief in austere or damaged ports.

The ship operates with a hybrid crew of military personnel and civil service mariners. The MILCREWs rotate for deployments and are based in San Diego, while the ship is homeported in Yokosuka under the operational control of U.S. 7th Fleet.

Military Sealift Command directs and supports operations for approximately 140 civilian-crewed ships that replenish U.S. Navy ships at sea, conduct specialized missions, preposition combat cargo worldwide, provide support services, and transport military equipment and supplies to deployed U.S. forces.

content:
【大紀元2026年11月16日訊】（大紀元記者鍾元台灣報導）中華民國外交部今年度訪賓接待預算較去年增加逾1.5億元（新台幣，以下同），遭立法院質疑成效並凍結1,500萬元，要求說明具體效益。外交部說明，預算增加主要是為了因應中共打壓，且台美、台加關係深化，使得相關邀訪及交流需求增加。
中華民國外交部115（2026）年度訪賓接待預算編列6億9,570萬1,000元，較114（2025）年度增加1億5,551萬元。
針對立委質疑，外交部未具體說明新增經費用途、執行策略及中長期規劃，也未提出邀訪成果等量化評估方式，凍結該項預算1,500萬元。
外交部書面報告說明，115年度訪賓接待預算較上一年度增加的主要考量，分別是因應中共壓縮台灣國際空間、掌握區域情勢及合作契機，以及成本上漲。
外交部表示，因應中共持續利誘與滲透台灣友邦及友台人士，壓縮台灣國際空間，須加強與各國決策圈與意見領袖聯繫，拓展各層級合作。隨著美國川普（特朗普）政府加強與拉美國家互動，外交部必須掌握區域情勢及合作契機，透過邀訪強化與友邦及友好非邦交國的關係；另外，台美、台加合作持續深化，各領域邀訪及交流需求也隨之增加。
此外，外交部指出，國際情勢、通貨膨脹、匯率及油價波動，也影響機票、膳宿、交通及保險等接待成本，其中機票為主要必要支出，須依航線供需及市場價格辦理。以北美地區為例，113（2024）年及114年度邀訪經費已漸不敷實際需求，因此115年度依邀訪計劃、既有執行情形及成本變動審慎增編。
針對邀訪具體成果，外交部說明，巴拉圭總統潘尼亞今年5月來台訪問，簽署《台巴刑事司法互助條約》、《台巴資安合作瞭解備忘錄》及《台巴主權AI算力中心投資案合作瞭解備忘錄》，深化雙邊司法、資安及智慧科技合作；巴拿馬國會議員今年2月率團來訪，對台灣政經發展印象深刻，促成巴拿馬國會在9月成立友台小組，共45位議員加入。
外交部將持續邀請美、加具政治影響力或發展潛力政要、政治幕僚及學者專家訪台，培植友台力量。去年度「邀訪計劃」以全額負擔訪問費用方式接待北美地區訪團，共計41團、345人。另外，外交部也落地接待自費或由商會自行籌組的訪團，拓展人脈，奠定長期合作基礎。

content:
中共央行再次調高外匯存款準備金率，鎖定美元流動性，以抑制人民幣升值。圖為中共央行。（Liu Jin / AFP / Getty Images）
【大紀元2026年11月15日訊】（大紀元記者任義綜合報導）年初至今，人民幣升值幅度加大，外貿出口企業利潤大減。在此大背景下，依賴出口拉動經濟的中共，不得不再次調高外匯存款準備金率，被指釋放出央行對人民幣匯率快速走強感到不安的信號。
今年以來，人民幣對美元匯率持續上漲。據Wind數據統計，今年以來，在岸與離岸人民幣對美元匯率年內最高點位均升破6.65，年內升值幅度近5%，創下逾四年來新高。高盛預測，未來12個月人民幣將升值至6.40元兌1美元。
11月15日，中共央行上調金融機構外匯存款準備金率，從4%上調至6%。這是近五年來，央行首次上調外匯存款準備金率。據央行的公告，上一次上調外匯存款準備金率是在2021年12月15日。
中共央行數據顯示，截至9月底，外匯存款達到創紀錄的1.2萬億美元，此次上調外匯存款準備金率預計鎖定約240億美元。
外匯存款準備金，是指金融機構按照規定將其吸收外匯存款的一定比例交存央行的存款。
據《上海證券報》等媒體11月15日報導，上調外匯存款準備金率，背後是人民幣對美元匯率延續升值態勢。東方金誠首席宏觀分析師王青表示，上調金融機構外匯存款準備金率，意味著銀行等金融機構需要籌集更多美元向央行繳存。這會導致境內市場美元流動性收緊，美元利率上行，削弱企業結匯需求，進而壓制人民幣升值動能。
中國民生銀行首席經濟學家溫彬說，此舉傳遞出明確的穩匯率政策信號，「相對於人民幣外匯市場日均超過8,000億美元的交易體量，這一規模本身並不足以實質性改變外匯供求格局。」
跨境金融研究院院長王志毅則認為，央行本輪逆週期調節在短期內將對人民幣升值起到緩衝作用，但不意味著升值行情就此結束。一方面，影響人民幣匯率走勢的因素較多，包括經濟基本面、美元走勢、跨境資金流動、國際收支等；另一方面，人民幣匯率無論是單邊快速升值還是單邊快速貶值都可能帶來風險。
路透社採訪的多數分析師認為，此舉釋放出央行對人民幣匯率快速走強感到不安的信號。
人民幣升值帶來的壓力，正壓縮中國出口企業的利潤。渣打銀行估算，人民幣實質有效匯率每升值1%，將導致出口企業平均利潤率下降約0.3個百分點。
據路透社日前報導，浙江寧波服裝出口商陳利峰（音譯）表示，人民幣升值使產品在歐洲市場變得更貴，幾乎吞噬了企業的利潤。
「這已經影響我們接單的能力，幾乎沒剩多少利潤了。如果人民幣繼續升值，我們將無法繼續經營。」陳利峰說。他經營的服裝貿易主要向歐洲出口。
福建福州和盛塑業的企業負責人陳秀俊也表示，國內「產能過剩和惡性競爭」迫使企業到海外尋找客戶，但人民幣升值又帶來新的壓力。他形容：「已經沒有地方可以躲了。」
路透社分析5,209家中國上市公司及9,733家海外企業的數據發現，中國企業今年上半年淨利潤率中位數只有4.9%，海外同業則達8.9%。據法國外貿銀行（Natixis）的另一項研究，中國電動汽車、電池、太陽能及風能設備、半導體等產業，利潤率僅約2%。

title: 大陸民眾加緊還債 分析：中共救樓市新規不及預期
summary: 中共為救樓市推出了40年房貸和對房貸貼息政策，但民眾正在加緊減少貸款、償還債務。(STR/AFP/Getty Images) 【大紀元2026年11月15日訊】（大紀元記者任義綜合報導）中國房地產市場低迷，中共為救樓市推出了40年房貸和對房貸貼息政策，但均不及預期。金融數據顯示，中國民眾正在加緊減少貸款、償還債務。 中共財政部、央行和金融監管總局此前聯合對外發布《關於實施居民購房貸款貼息政策的通知》，稱自2026年10月1日起，實施居民購房貸款貼息政策，政策實施期暫定1年。

中共為救樓市推出了40年房貸和對房貸貼息政策，但民眾正在加緊減少貸款、償還債務。(STR/AFP/Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月15日訊】（大紀元記者任義綜合報導）中國房地產市場低迷，中共為救樓市推出了40年房貸和對房貸貼息政策，但均不及預期。金融數據顯示，中國民眾正在加緊減少貸款、償還債務。
中共財政部、央行和金融監管總局此前聯合對外發布《關於實施居民購房貸款貼息政策的通知》，稱自2026年10月1日起，實施居民購房貸款貼息政策，政策實施期暫定1年。
據報導，這是中央財政首次直接針對個人商業性住房貸款推出貼息政策，財政部門給予年化1個百分點貼息，按照目前首套住房商業性個人住房貸款利率水平，相當於優惠了利率三分之一，貼息期限最長5年。對於一筆長期限的100萬元（人民幣，下同）商業性個人住房貸款，貼息政策最多可幫助借款人累計減少付息近5萬元。
不過目前中共上述房貸貼息的拉動作用並未顯現，居民信貸整體延續收縮態勢。中共央行最新金融數據顯示，10月新增人民幣貸款減少1,000億元，同比多減3,200億元（去年同期也在減少）。其中，住戶貸款減少4,300億元，同比多減696億元。
分項數據顯示，居民部門短期貸款減少2,700億元，同比少減166億元，中長期貸款減少1,563億元，同比多減863億元。
據《第一財經》等媒體11月15日報導，民生銀行首席經濟學家溫彬分析，購房貼息政策效應偏弱，居民觀望情緒濃厚，加槓桿購房意願尚未修復，按揭投放持續承壓。
光大證券金融業首席分析師王一峰也認為，預期偏弱背景下，居民置業觀望情緒較濃，加槓桿購房意願、能力未見扭轉，按揭投放持續承壓。
居民貸款可分為經營性貸款、住房貸款與非住房消費貸款。金融數據顯示，截至2026年三季度末，個人住房貸款餘額35.91萬億元，同比下降4.1%，前三季度減少1.10萬億元；經營性貸款餘額25.64萬億元，同比增長1.7%，前三季度增加5,383億元；不含個人住房貸款的消費性貸款餘額20.69萬億元，同比下降2.8%，前三季度減少4,736億元。
住房貸款自2025年二季度起，連續六個季度淨增量為負數，遠超此前最長三個季度的收縮週期；非住房消費貸款連續四個季度淨增量為負數。
另據中國國家金融與發展實驗室發布的《2026年三季度宏觀槓桿率報告》，2026年三季度，居民部門槓桿率從2024年一季度的62.3%下降至2026年三季度的56.4%，累計去槓桿幅度接近6個百分點。2026年以來，居民部門債務增速進入負值區間，前三季度增速分別為-0.4%、-1.3%和-2.0%，降幅逐季度擴大。
時政觀察人士夏言表示，過去幾十年，中國民眾的債務幾乎一直在增長，而「債務增速為負」意味著整個社會背負的總債務餘額比去年同期變少了，也就是大家償還貸款總額，超過了銀行發放出去的貸款總額。今年以來，各季度數據負值擴大，說明居民償還債務和減少貸款的趨勢不僅沒有停止，反而在每個季度持續加快。

中期失败后，特朗普希望在习近平和普京峰会上展示权力

（左起）俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京、唐纳德·特朗普和习近平将于 11 月 19 日举行峰会，北京称此次峰会具有“开创性意义”。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 16 日 下午 04:55
更新于 2026 年 11 月 16 日 05:32
在经历了中期选举失败和英伟达丑闻之后，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在国内表现疲弱，他希望在国外展示实力并重申自己的领导地位。
11 月 19 日在深圳举行的三边会议将重点讨论伊朗、无核化和贸易问题，而乌克兰可能会被排除在外，这引起了基辅和西方首都的担忧。
尽管有关中美贸易、人工智能芯片和出口管制的谈判仍然紧张，预计不会取得重大突破，中国可能会利用这次会议来提升习近平主席的全球形象。
北京 — — 唐纳德·特朗普即将与习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京举行史无前例的峰会，他在国内政治上被削弱，但也许更渴望在海外展示自己的权力。
最近几周，美国总统遭受了双重打击，这可能给世界上最大核大国的聚会蒙上阴影：共和党在美国中期选举中惨败，以及导致黄仁勋失去人工智能芯片制造商英伟达领导者职位的丑闻。
选举结果突显了国内对与伊朗的战争及其造成的更高燃料成本的愤怒。尽管中俄两国在冲突问题上存在分歧，特朗普仍寻求加深与中俄两国的关系。
特朗普的批评者变得更加大胆，其中包括对华鹰派人士，他们表示特朗普与习近平的关系过于密切。
在黄仁勋与一名疑似中国间谍的恋情被曝光后，黄仁勋被免职，他与特朗普的关系以及他作为人工智能行业最直言不讳的向中国出售先进芯片的倡导者的角色受到了更严格的审查。
特朗普讨好俄罗斯总统、批评乌克兰总统泽连斯基的做法也招致了批评。
当他在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）领导人峰会以及与中国领导人的一对一会谈期间与习近平和普京坐下来时，所有这些都可能使他的讨价还价立场变得复杂。
但特朗普在华盛顿地位的削弱可能同时将他推向一个他拥有更多控制权的舞台：与外国势力的高风险外交。
美国前亚太经合组织大使唐科表示，面对“跛脚鸭”地位的前景，他的前任们经常转向外交政策，以此作为提醒美国盟友和竞争对手特朗普仍然是总司令的机会。
“毫无疑问，总统将寻求利用这次访问重申领导力和权威，展示他的政治家能力，并在国际舞台上炫耀，”目前在华盛顿咨询公司亚洲集团工作的唐说。
一位不愿透露姓名的高级政府官员表示，预计特朗普将利用三方会议讨论伊朗战争，但将避免讨论乌克兰问题。
中国外交部 11 月 16 日证实，继白宫早些时候宣布三方会谈将于 11 月 19 日举行。
外交部发言人毛宁表示，这次会议将具有“开创性意义”。

Trump looks to flex power at Xi, Putin summit after midterm loss
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
(From left) Presidents Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are set to hold a summit on Nov 19 that will have what Beijing describes as “ground-breaking significance”.
Published Nov 16, 2026, 04:55 PM
Updated Nov 16, 2026, 05:32 PM
Weakened at home after midterm losses and the Nvidia scandal, US President Donald Trump wants to show strength abroad and reassert his leadership.
The Nov 19 trilateral in Shenzhen will focus on Iran, denuclearisation and trade, while Ukraine is likely to be left out, raising concern in Kyiv and Western capitals.
China may use the meeting to boost President Xi Jingping’s global image, even as talks over US-China trade, AI chips and export controls remain tense, with no major breakthrough expected.
BEIJING – Donald Trump is arriving at an unprecedented summit meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin politically weakened at home, yet perhaps even more eager to flex his power abroad.
The US president has suffered twin blows in recent weeks that threaten to cloud the gathering of the world’s largest nuclear powers: Republicans’ crippling defeats in the US midterm elections and the scandal that cost Jensen Huang his job leading artificial intelligence chipmaker Nvidia.
The election result highlighted domestic anger over the war with Iran, and the higher fuel costs it caused. Trump has sought to deepen relationships with his Chinese and Russian counterparts despite their differences over the conflict.
Trump’s critics have been emboldened, including China hawks who say he has cultivated too close a relationship with Xi.
Huang’s ouster, following the revelation of his affair with a suspected Chinese spy, heightened scrutiny of his ties to Trump, as well as his role as the AI industry’s most vocal advocate for selling advanced chips to China.
Trump’s efforts to curry favour with his Russian counterpart, and criticise Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, have also drawn criticism.
All of that may complicate his bargaining position when he sits down with Xi and Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit in Shenzhen, China, as well as his one-on-one talk with the Chinese leader.
But Trump’s weakened position in Washington may simultaneously be pushing him towards an arena where he has more control: high-stakes diplomacy with foreign powers.
Facing down the prospect of lame-duck status, his predecessors have often pivoted to foreign policy as a chance to remind America’s allies and rivals that Trump is still commander-in-chief, said Kurt Tong, a former US ambassador for APEC.
“The president will undoubtedly be seeking to use this trip to reassert leadership, authority, demonstrate his statesmanship capabilities and essentially show off on the international stage,” said Tong, who is now at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.
Trump is expected to use the three-way meeting to discuss the war in Iran, but will avoid discussing Ukraine, according to a senior administration official who briefed reporters on condition of anonymity.
China’s Foreign Ministry confirmed on Nov 16 that the trilateral will take place on Nov 19 following an earlier White House announcement.
The meeting will have “ground-breaking significance”, said ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning.
It could bolster China’s standing as a global power while also giving Trump an opportunity to project strength abroad as he grapples with low approval ratings and the prospect of investigations by a Democrat-led Congress.
He has said he wants to discuss denuclearisation with the two leaders, an issue he has sought to tackle with them since his first term, without success. China has long resisted trilateral talks around nuclear arms, as its stockpile is far smaller than the US and Russia’s.
Still, a meeting between Trump and Putin is likely to set off alarm bells in Kyiv and Western capitals, handing the Russian leader a chance to shape any negotiated peace deal on favourable terms for Moscow – without Ukraine present to determine its own future.
Trump has taken a defiant tone in the wake of his electoral loss, elevating hardliner Stephen Miller to the role of White House chief of staff and threatening to block Democrats’ agenda. That is an indication that leaders in Asia are unlikely to see a chastened US president on the world stage.
He has also indicated the Huang saga is unlikely to change his efforts to cultivate his relationship with Xi. A senior administration official said Trump had no intention of raising the issue with Xi, suggesting the focus would be on economic cooperation.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has faced accusations of delaying export controls and shielding Nvidia from restrictions on advanced chip shipments to China, is expected to be in Shenzhen, according to people familiar with the matter.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is also planning to make the trip, the people said, as is Secretary of State Marco Rubio, according to the State Department.
Trump’s agenda includes a stop in Manila to meet leaders of the Association of South-east Asian Nations summit before his meeting with Xi and Putin.
Xi and Trump’s prior meetings in 2026 were high on pomp and circumstance but low on substance, and White House officials have not forecast major breakthroughs on trade or other policy priorities during his next summit.
A “30 billion for 30 billion” reciprocal tariff-reduction deal, agreed in principle at previous summits,is still being hashed out.
“All the signals coming out of the White House are that this trip is a courtesy call,” said Edgard Kagan, a former US ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
Beijing may be more interested in highlighting Xi’s role as the chair of APEC than Trump’s attendance.
“They don’t want Trump to step on Xi’s overall message of leadership,” Kagan added.
Washington and Beijing are expected to focus on the year-long trade truce between the world’s top economies that is set to expire in January. It is unclear if a new extension will be hashed out at this meeting. In December, Xi is set to attend the Group of 20 summit in the US.
The pact was initially struck in Busan, South Korea, in October 2025, where both sides agreed to suspend additional 24% levies while leaving a 10% rate in place. China also agreed to allow the export of some rare earth minerals essential for everything from fighter jets to electric cars, a commitment the US says has not been implemented fully.
Trump is also set to meet leaders of the Quad alliance, which includes the US, Japan, India and Australia, in Manila in the group’s first leader-level meeting since his return to office.
The group, formed to counter China’s growing influence in the Indo-Pacific region, is likely to touch on the war in Iran, which has led to global oil supply disruptions due to closures in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US and its allies have agreed to jointly identify and protect artificial intelligence technologies and supply chains considered vulnerable to China, the Financial Times reported over the weekend.
The State Department said in a statement on Nov 15 that the US and nine other countries will seek to safeguard technologies and systems essential to AI supply chains, without naming China.
Spy scandal and midterm defeat heat up Trump’s Asia visit
Trump’s tariffs cast shadow over APEC talks
AI and business deals are also expected to be on the agenda. Despite Trump’s comments, the meeting could be further strained by the fallout from the Nvidia scandal.
Huang’s downfall at the company he founded will deprive Trump of a travel partner who accompanied him on his last China trip and attended the state dinner with Xi at the White House two months ago. China has called the spying allegations a “smear”.
Some Republican lawmakers have pressed Trump to take a more aggressive stance toward Beijing, including greater export controls to curb the flow of semiconductors to China.
House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters at the Capitol that there is “a developing consensus in Congress” about tightening curbs on sending advanced models to Chinese customers.
One option would be widening curbs to capture subsidiaries majority-owned by already-sanctioned firms. The so-called 50% rule that has been suspended until January is regarded by some in Washington as the key to closing a major loophole.
Greer told CNBC he did not expect export controls to come up during the APEC trip, noting that while the Chinese may raise the issue, it’s a matter of “internal affairs”.
“Conversations about economic security and export controls are not things we negotiate with the Chinese,” Greer said. BLOOMBERG

人工智能功能将用于监控人群和读取车牌。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 16 日 下午 03:06
更新于 2026 年 11 月 16 日 03:28
香港已在 SmartView 旗下的闭路电视网络中推出人工智能面部识别技术，称这将有助于国家安全、预防犯罪和追踪嫌疑人。
警方表示，已经安装了约 5,000 个摄像头，与近 2,200 起案件和 2,800 多人被捕有关，计划到 2028 年安装到 60,000 个摄像头。
此举引发了人们对隐私和滥用的担忧。居民和人权组织对持续监控、虚假匹配和透明度薄弱提出警告，而官员则表示该系统“不会被滥用”。
香港 — 11 月 16 日，香港在其摄像头监控系统中推出了人工智能面部识别功能，以国家安全和预防犯罪的名义扩大了对公共场所的监控。
自2019年大规模民主抗议活动席卷香港以来，中国加强了对香港的控制，对这个金融中心实施了国家安全法，批评者称此举平息了异议。
警察局长 Joe Chow 周末表示，新的人工智能工具是名为 SmartView 的警方行动的一部分，将成为“守法公民的保障”，并增强现有监控系统的功能，并宣布将于 11 月 16 日推出。
安全主管 Chris Tang 将于 2025 年向立法者表示，人工智能功能将用于监控人群和读取车牌，并且“自然会应用于人类，例如追踪犯罪嫌疑人”。
自 2024 年推出 SmartView 以来，警方已在香港各地安装了约 5,000 个闭路电视 (CCTV) 摄像头，警方利用这些摄像头解决了近 2,200 起案件并逮捕了 2,800 多人。
根据提交给立法机关的文件，当局计划到 2028 年将摄像头数量增加到 60,000 个。
40多岁的香港金融工作者李先生出于安全考虑拒绝透露全名，他告诉法新社，他担心人工智能监控可能被滥用。
“任何地方都没有秘密，（许多工具）已经收集了你的数据和面部图像，”他说。
另一位名叫周六周的居民则不太担心，他告诉法新社，“大陆城市已经有很多这样的（人工智能驱动的闭路电视），人们已经习惯了它们”。
他补充说，官员“必须公开”他们对相关数据的使用，以保持透明度。
周局长11月15日对当地媒体表示，“我们理解很多人可能对此感到担忧”，但新制度“不会被滥用”。
中国大陆已经在其监控系统中大规模使用人工智能，引起了国际人权组织和非政府组织的担忧。
澳大利亚战略政策研究所于 2025 年发布的一份报告警告说，中国政府使用人工智能工具使其能够“实现审查自动化、加强监视并先发制人地压制异议”。
类似的技术也被其他地方采用，包括英国。批评者认为，它授予政府不受限制的侵犯隐私的权力。
人们还担心虚假匹配会导致错误逮捕以及摄像机周围的透明度。

Hong Kong rolls out AI facial recognition across CCTV network
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
The AI functions will be used to monitor crowds and read licence plates.
Published Nov 16, 2026, 03:06 PM
Updated Nov 16, 2026, 03:28 PM
Hong Kong has rolled out AI facial recognition across its CCTV network under SmartView, saying it will help national security, crime prevention and tracking suspects.
Police say about 5,000 cameras are already installed, linked to nearly 2,200 cases and more than 2,800 arrests, with plans to reach 60,000 cameras by 2028.
The move has raised privacy and misuse fears. Residents and rights groups warn about constant monitoring, false matches and weak transparency, while officials say the system “won’t be abused”.
HONG KONG – Hong Kong rolled out AI-powered facial recognition functions across its camera surveillance system on Nov 16, expanding monitoring of public spaces in the name of national security and crime-prevention.
China has tightened control over Hong Kong since huge pro-democracy protests swept the city in 2019, imposing a national security law on the finance hub that critics say has quelled dissent.
The new artificial intelligence tools, part of a police operation dubbed SmartView, will be a “safeguard for law-abiding citizens” and boost the capabilities of existing surveillance systems, police commissioner Joe Chow said over the weekend, announcing the Nov 16 rollout.
Security chief Chris Tang told lawmakers in 2025 that the AI functions will be used to monitor crowds and read licence plates, and “will naturally be applied to people, such as tracking a criminal suspect”.
The police have already installed roughly 5,000 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras across Hong Kong since SmartView launched in 2024, crediting their use in solving nearly 2,200 cases and more than 2,800 arrests.
The authorities plan to increase the number of cameras to 60,000 by 2028, according to documents submitted to the legislature.
Li, a Hong Kong finance worker in his 40s who declined to give his full name due to safety concerns, told AFP he was worried about the potential misuse of AI-powered surveillance.
“There are no secrets left anywhere, (many tools) have already collected your data and facial images,” he said.
Another resident named Saturday Zhou was less concerned, telling AFP that “there are already plenty of these (AI-powered CCTVs) in mainland cities and people have got used to them”.
Officials “must be open” about their use of the relevant data in order to maintain transparency, he added.
Commissioner Chow told the local media on Nov 15 that “we understand that many people may be concerned about this” but the new system “won’t be abused”.
Mainland China already uses AI in its surveillance systems on a massive scale, drawing concern from international rights groups and non-governmental organisations.
A report released in 2025 by the Australian Strategic Policy Institute warned the Chinese government’s use of AI tools enabled it to “automate censorship, enhance surveillance and pre‑emptively suppress dissent”.
Similar technology has also been adopted elsewhere, including in Britain. Critics argue that it grants the government unchecked power to invade privacy.
Concerns have also been raised over false matches leading to wrongful arrests and transparency surrounding the cameras.
In 2024, the European Union banned “the use of ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement”, with some exceptions. AFP

美国和中国保持着脆弱的贸易休战，但华盛顿希望中国履行其承诺，并可能对先进芯片施加压力。
特朗普可能会寻求在朝鲜和军备控制问题上取得胜利，而习近平则希望推迟美国在台湾和贸易问题上采取更强硬的立场。
北京/华盛顿 — — 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普本周将前往亚洲，因中期选举惨败和中国间谍指控而感到震惊，这些指控增加了他与北京强大领导人习近平最近一次面对面的风险。
特朗普将于11月17日首先访问马尼拉，与东南亚和其他地区领导人举行会晤，然后飞往深圳参加亚太经合组织（APEC）论坛，在那里他将与中国国家主席会面，并与习近平和俄罗斯总统普京进行三方会谈。
由于中美之间脆弱的贸易战休战期延长至 2027 年初，而特朗普与习近平将于 12 月在迈阿密举行的 G20 峰会上举行更多会谈，一些分析人士最初将深圳会议视为一次低风险峰会。
但在 11 月 3 日的中期选举中，特朗普所在的共和党遭到强烈反对，并批评他的政府未能根据与特朗普关系密切的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋与一名疑似中国间谍有染的情报采取行动，这些都让这些预期变得混乱。
伦敦智库托尼·布莱尔研究所(Tony Blair Institute)的中国问题高级政策顾问鲁比·奥斯曼(Ruby Osman)表示：“由于担心市场反应或选举影响的理由减少，（特朗普）可能更愿意考虑破坏性措施。”
华盛顿已经在会议前表达了这​​样的意愿，敦促中国履行一年前特朗普和习近平达成的休战协议中做出的承诺。
中国分析人士表示，他们特别担心英伟达事件，包括有关受限制的半导体被转移给中国客户的指控，现在将强化美国对中国的态度。
美国众议院议长迈克·约翰逊上周表示，丑闻发生后，国会就进一步限制中国获得先进芯片达成了越来越多的共识，预计民主党在一月份接管众议院和参议院多数席位时将在这个问题上大力施压。
中国表示，美国捏造了间谍故事，为技术封锁辩护。
南京大学国际问题研究所所长朱峰表示，这场争端也可能加速世界两个超级大国之间的“人工智能脱钩”，尽管它们试图合作减轻该技术的风险。
一位不愿透露姓名的美国高级政府表示，预计特朗普不会直接向习近平提出间谍指控，并补充说英伟达的情况“实际上不应对此次访问产生任何影响”。
特朗普可能不想与中国挑起新的争斗，而是想把重点放在遗产建设上，例如与北京和莫斯科达成无核化协议，或者确保与朝鲜秘密领导人金正恩再次会面。

Spy scandal and midterm defeat heat up Trump’s Asia visit

Trump visits Asia after midterm losses and spy claims, making his talks with Xi Jinping more tense.
The US and China keep a fragile trade truce, but Washington wants China to meet its promises and may press on advanced chips.
Trump may seek legacy wins on North Korea and arms control, while Xi wants to delay a tougher US line on Taiwan and trade.
BEIJING/WASHINGTON – US President Donald Trump heads to Asia this week, reeling from a midterm election drubbing and Chinese spy allegations that have raised the stakes for his latest face-to-face with Beijing’s powerful leader, Xi Jinping.
Trump will first visit Manila for meetings with South-east Asian and other regional leaders on Nov 17 before jetting to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, where he will meet the Chinese President and hold three-way discussions with Xi and Russia’s Vladimir Putin.
With a fragile trade-war truce between the US and China extended to early 2027, and more Trump-Xi talks due in December at the G20 in Miami, some analysts had initially billed the Shenzhen meeting as a low-stakes summit.
But a backlash against Trump’s Republican Party in the Nov 3 midterms and criticism that his administration failed to act on intelligence that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, who has close ties to Trump, had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, have muddied those expectations.
“With less reason to worry about market reactions or electoral fallout, (Trump) may be more willing to consider disruptive measures,” said Ruby Osman, a senior policy adviser on China at the Tony Blair Institute, a London-based think-tank.
Washington has already signalled such willingness ahead of the meeting, urging China to live up to its commitments made under the truce agreed between Trump and Xi a year ago.
Chinese analysts say they are particularly concerned that the Nvidia saga, including allegations that restricted semiconductors were diverted to Chinese customers, will now harden US attitudes towards China.
US House Speaker Mike Johnson said last week there was growing consensus in Congress on further limiting Chinese access to advanced chips after the scandal, and Democrats are expected to press hard on the issue when they take over the House and Senate majorities in January.
China has said the US has fabricated the spy narrative to justify a technological blockade.
Zhu Feng, director of the Institute of International Studies at Nanjing University, said the spat could also speed up “the decoupling of AI” between the world’s two superpowers even as they try to cooperate on mitigating the technology’s risks.
Trump is not expected to directly raise the spy allegations with Xi, one senior US administration said on condition of anonymity, adding that the Nvidia situation “should not really have any bearing on the trip”.
Rather than picking fresh fights with China, Trump may want to focus on legacy-building endeavours such as denuclearisation agreements with Beijing and Moscow, or securing another meeting with North Korea’s secretive leader, Kim Jong Un.
Trump sees the unprecedented summit with Xi and Putin as possibly providing movement towards an agreement on nuclear arms control. But that is a non-starter for China, which has far fewer warheads than the others, Chinese analysts said.
Trump may also seek to enlist Putin and Xi’s support in setting up a future meeting with Kim, who has close ties to the Chinese and Russian leaders.
The president will be focused on “building his legacy”, said Victor Cha at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, a US think-tank. A big part of that is his North Korea diplomacy, which he has devoted a lot of time to over his two terms, Cha added.
The proposed three-way meeting has drawn comparisons, particularly in Russia, with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the US, Britain and the Soviet Union that formalised spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-World War II order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
Such a framing is particularly worrisome for Ukraine, engaged in a four-year war with Russia. Trump is not expected to raise Ukraine at the meeting, the senior US official said.

Trump’s tariffs cast shadow over APEC talks
Xi could also seek to take advantage of Trump’s political weakness after his election humbling, analysts say.
Top of Beijing’s wish list is ensuring that the US president does not approve a US$14 billion (S$18 billion) arms package to Taiwan, which China claims as its own. Trump has said he is holding the arms back as a “negotiating chip” with China.
But with China’s export engine humming, simply buying time may be enough for Beijing, said Jonathan Czin, a foreign policy analyst at the Brookings Institution, a US-based think-tank.
“Xi just needs Trump to remain reluctant to revert towards a more competitive posture toward China for as long as possible. China will take whatever time it can get to fortify itself for the next round in the contest,” said Czin, who formerly worked at the Central Intelligence Agency and as director for China at the US National Security Council.
Beijing will be acutely aware that whoever succeeds Trump when his term ends in two years time, may be less accommodating, said Czin and Osman.
Trump’s Democratic predecessor, Joe Biden, repeatedly angered China with comments over human rights issues and a pledge that the US would defend Taiwan if Beijing attacked. Many of Trump’s potential Republican successors, such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio, are also seen as more hawkish on China.
Both leaders will also be wary of reigniting a trade row that threatened to tank the global economy and financial markets in 2025, said Kurt Tong, a former senior State Department official now with the Asia Group think-tank.
Despite the frustration the US has voiced on Chinese implementation of the terms of the truce, Tong expects it will be further extended beyond its Jan 10 expiration.
“The two sides are quite incentivised to maintain this fragile stability... despite also having some disagreements,” added senior China analyst Chim Lee at the Economist Intelligence Unit.
“They both have quite a lot to lose.” REUTERS

Trump’s tariffs cast shadow over APEC talks
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
APEC’s 21 members gathering in Shenzhen include the US and China, as well as Japan, Russia, Canada, Mexico, Australia and Indonesia.
Published Nov 16, 2026, 12:46 PM
Updated Nov 16, 2026, 04:34 PM
APEC talks in Shenzhen are overshadowed by US-China rivalry and Donald Trump’s tariff war, which has left the summit with a limited agenda.
Trump has kept or added tariffs on many economies, including duties of up to “12.5%” on 60 economies, while sector tariffs on steel, cars and timber remain.
Countries are seeking new trade partners to cut reliance on the US, but RCEP and other deals offer only limited protection because enforcement is weak.
SHENZHEN – Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) nations account for just over half of global commerce, but geopolitical rivalries and US President Donald Trump’s trade war – even after a midterm drubbing – mean an agenda of limited ambition at this week’s summit.
All located around the Pacific Rim, the organisation’s 21 members gathering in Shenzhen include the US and China, as well as Japan, Russia, Canada, Mexico, Australia and Indonesia.
But “having China serve as host in an institution that includes the United States and Russia has not been a recipe for success”, said Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore.
“All three are at odds with one another and geopolitical rivalries that cross many members have made cooperation on even relatively benign topics harder than ever,” Elms wrote in a research note.
Important figures including US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent skipped an APEC finance ministers’ meeting in Hong Kong in October, depriving other members of “the opportunity to connect to a key official from the United States”, Elms said.
China has also been making “unhelpful changes” to APEC processes, like moving some meetings online and not confirming until very late in the process the timings of some key events, she added.
At the same time, there is no sign of a reversal in Trump’s tariff blitz, even after the Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections on Nov 3.
The US Supreme Court struck down a host of Trump’s Customs duties in February.
But Washington has since cited inadequate efforts to combat forced labour as grounds for imposing new tariffs – as high as 12.5% – on 60 economies, including APEC members in Asia and Latin America.
Meanwhile, sector-specific tariffs on steel, cars and timber remain in effect.
Trump is “doubling down”, said Joshua Kurlantzick, senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, and Congress “can’t do much about Trump’s trade and tariffs, and I don’t think Trump is going to change”.
“He doesn’t care also about whether his policies impact GOP favourability, so that kind of makes him unleashed to do whatever he wants in a way,” Kurlantzick told AFP, referring to the Republicans.
This has added to the impetus for other countries to deepen trade relations without the world’s biggest economy.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Nov 14 that Ottawa had concluded negotiations for a free trade pact with the Philippines. He added that a broader agreement was also in the works with the entirety of the 11-member ASEAN.
The pacts were “part of a strategy of developing a dense web of reliable partners to create more opportunities... and reducing our relative reliance on the United States”, Carney said.
Brazil’s newly re-elected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, while not an APEC member, sounded a similar note at the ASEAN gathering in Manila on Nov 15.
“Brazil has learnt an extraordinary lesson after the US decided to impose tariffs (on other countries),” Lula told reporters.
“Instead of weeping or begging the US government... to have pity on us, we decided to look for other partners for us to sell to and for us to buy from,” he said, noting that trade with Indonesia and Vietnam had jumped 15% and 13% respectively.
The Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) – a free trade agreement encompassing China, South-east Asian nations and other regional partners such as Japan, Australia and South Korea – has meanwhile set long-term targets for tariff reductions.
However, the agreement’s provisions “suffer from weaker enforcement and dispute settlement mechanisms”, said Nick Marro, principal Asia economist at the Economist Intelligence Unit.
“While the drive to expand and deepen RCEP will stay, the pact will offer middle powers relatively limited shelter in an increasingly fractious geopolitical landscape – especially amid rising US protectionism and the continued global spillover of China’s economic imbalances,” he told AFP. AFP

夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《国防一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

中国湖新落成的 300 加仑能量混合器预计到 2027 年 6 月达到生产能力，与行业合作伙伴一起为 WDU-36/B 战斧弹头建立另一个美国海军运营的来源。 NAWCWD 新闻稿 一年前，海军空战中心武器部门的能量学团队从博物馆中取出了一个战斧弹头盒。该团队将炸药和火箭推进剂混合在一起，并将其装入海军武器中。他们清理了箱子。他们将PBXN-107炸药混合并填充到WDU-36/B弹头中。测试、成像和 X 射线证实团队正确填充了它。今年秋天，同一个团队填充了七颗首枚战斧弹头，这是新生产商建造的第一批用于检查的装置。能量处理部门负责人赞恩·戈德特表示，一旦通过，它们将成为“中国湖”的第一批生产弹头。这些子弹是由一台 150 加仑的 China Lake 搅拌机生产的，该搅拌机已经运行了数十年。 11 月 9 日，NAWCWD 在重建的汽车装配厂内为一台新的 300 加仑搅拌机剪彩。一旦在 2027 年 6 月左右上线，混合器将使团队达到生产率。目标是在雷神公司需要弹头之前准备好弹头，帮助确保战斧式弹头持续、准时地交付给舰队。 NAWCWD 战斧技术项目办公室主任帕特里夏·霍托（Patricia Hottowe）表示，“战斧”可以让舰艇和潜艇从安全水域、远离敌人射程的地方开火。

【原文 English Original】
A newly inaugurated 300-gallon energetics mixer at China Lake is slated to reach production rate by June 2027, establishing an additional U.S. Navy-run source for WDU-36/B Tomahawk warheads alongside industry partners. NAWCWD press release A year ago, the energetics team at Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division pulled a Tomahawk warhead case out of a museum. The team mixes explosives and rocket propellants and loads them into Navy weapons. They cleaned the case. They mixed PBXN-107 explosive and filled the WDU-36/B warhead. Testing, imaging and X-rays confirmed the team filled it correctly. This fall, the same team filled seven first-article Tomahawk warheads, the first units a new producer builds for inspection. Once they pass, they become China Lake’s first production warheads, said Zane Goedert, head of the Energetics Processing Branch. Those rounds came off a 150-gallon mixer China Lake has run for decades. On Nov. 9, NAWCWD cut the ribbon on a new 300-gallon mixer in the rebuilt Motor Assembly Compound. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let the team reach production rate. The goal is warheads ready before Raytheon needs them, helping ensure continuous, on-time Tomahawk deliveries to the fleet. Patricia Hottowe, director of the Tomahawk Technical Project Office at NAWCWD, said Tomahawk lets ships and submarines fire from safe waters, out of an enemy’s range. “Having an adequate stockpile of those for a peer or near-peer adversary is critical to the nation’s defense,” Hottowe said. In August, the Navy awarded Raytheon a $22.9 billion contract to accelerate Tomahawk production. Faster production calls for more warhead capacity, said Ryan Hunter, head of the Propulsion and Energetics Division. Navy labs at China Lake and at Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division in Maryland said they could do the work. But key parts and materials can take up to a year to arrive. During the demonstration build, the team also found the warhead specification needed a major update. Hottowe said the team spent much of the past year updating the specification and the approved supplier list. The Navy’s technical authority for the warhead must approve each new supplier. Every future producer, Navy or industry, must build to that specification. NAWCWD also bought long-lead materials ahead of the multiyear contract. That puts material on hand sooner. Hottowe said the team took on the work alongside its day jobs, with little added staff so far. That is changing. More than a dozen new hires are joining the team. Goedert said they will train under experienced technicians on safety, quality and procedures for about a year before working on their own. Goedert said loading the warhead is the easiest part. Buying materials, bringing on people and getting answers are harder. Hunter said the challenge comes from a system built for fixed multiyear schedules. Now that system must move faster on a shorter clock. NAWCWD Executive Director Dan Carreño often sums up the problem in one line: “Weapons take too long, cost too much, and are irrelevant when they get there.” The chemistry rests on decades of practice. The branch has filled warheads for SLAM-ER, a Navy air-launched missile, since the mid-1990s. Goedert said his team routinely turns one-of-a-kind prototypes around on short timelines. That experience let the team move faster on Tomahawk. Raytheon builds Tomahawk as the prime contractor. General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems machines the warhead cases. L3Harris loads them with explosive today. Guests gather in the large mix bay to watch a demonstration of a new 300-gallon mixer after its ribbon cutting at the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory, Nov. 9, 2026. Once online around June 2027, the mixer will let Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division’s energetics team reach production rate on Tomahawk warheads for the fleet. (U.S. Navy photo by Michael L. Smith) Rear Adm. Eric Gardner, principal deputy for the Portfolio Acquisition Executive Munitions, spoke at the ribbon cutting. He said the first-article warheads lay the groundwork for China Lake to become an additional source of Tomahawk warhead production. “At PAE Munitions, we know that increasing weapons production takes more than contracts and funding,” Gardner said. “It takes people, infrastructure, materials, and strong partnerships across our Navy, our warfare centers and industry.” In September, L3Harris and NAWCWD signed a multiyear public-private partnership to manufacture missile components. Under it, Hunter said, NAWCWD plans to produce a portion of the Tomahawk warheads. Carreño called China Lake’s energetics operation a pilot plant that will keep doing developmental testing. When industry needs NAWCWD, he said, the command now has “the legs and the horsepower to go augment.” Inside NAWCWD, the warhead effort tied the Tomahawk Technical Project Office tightly to the energetics team. Hunter said he has never seen a closer partnership in his career. China Lake’s plant layout adds speed. “Because our plant is dispersed and because we will be curing the warheads in a different area than we’re casting them, we’re able to do simultaneous processes that will get higher throughput,” Hunter said. The plant’s newest buildings grew out of a rebuild. The July 2019 earthquakes destroyed three energetics compounds in the Salt Wells area of the China Lake Propulsion Laboratory. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command broke ground on their replacements, known as the trio, in April 2022. The Nov. 9 ceremony celebrated the trio. Goedert said the team designed the Motor Assembly Compound to cut handling. Large rocket motors risk damage each time crews move them after casting. The same layout will speed warhead work. The new mixer, built by B&P Littleford, works much like a kitchen stand mixer, Goedert said. It is built for thick propellants and explosives. The mixer’s bowl will weigh close to 20,000 pounds. Today, crews mix in one building and cast in another, about half a mile away. In the compound’s large mix bay, the bowl will move across the room into a lift. An hourlong move will drop to 15 minutes. Those minutes count. Once mixed, these explosives start to set. Depending on the mix, crews have a couple of hours to eight or nine hours to cast it. The new layout will give back about 45 minutes of that window. Even the lift is a China Lake design. Before the team had one, workers hoisted the 150-gallon mixer’s 4,000-pound bowl and worked beneath the suspended load. Eric Wooding, a mechanical engineer, helped design a lift for that bowl years ago. “It was an idea of some people here and nobody would bid it. So we just decided to do it ourselves,” Wooding said. China Lake’s machine shop built the frame and parts. The lift worked from the start and has stayed in regular service since 2020. When the 300-gallon mixer went in, the team told the vendor to base the larger lift’s design on that concept. Hunter said the team is ready to “stand in the gap” when the Navy calls. “When we successfully complete this warhead production and ultimately return it to industry, where production belongs,” Hunter said, “we’ll be ready to take on the next challenge.” The post U.S. Navy Expands Tomahawk Warhead Production Capacity at China Lake appeared first on Naval News .

title: SUBPAC Commander Warns of Rapid Expansion in Chinese and Russian Submarine Fleets
zh_title: SUBPAC指挥官警告中国和俄罗斯潜艇舰队的快速扩张
summary: 在海军潜艇联盟 2026 年年度研讨会上的一系列演讲中，美国太平洋舰队潜艇部队司令克里斯·卡瓦诺 (Chris Cavanaugh) 就太平洋地区对手的发展和活动状况发表了讲话，强调了美国海军潜艇舰队面临的关键威胁。中国海军潜艇新型09IIIB型核潜艇，在中国社交媒体上分享的编辑图像。在考虑对美国海军的挑战时，RADM 卡瓦诺重申了中华人民共和国中国人民解放军海军（PLAN）作为印度-太平洋地区最大威胁的地位
content:
在海军潜艇联盟 2026 年年度研讨会上的一系列演讲中，美国太平洋舰队潜艇部队司令克里斯·卡瓦诺 (Chris Cavanaugh) 就太平洋地区对手的发展和活动状况发表了讲话，强调了美国海军潜艇舰队面临的关键威胁。中国海军潜艇新型09IIIB型核潜艇，在中国社交媒体上分享的编辑图像。 RADM 卡瓦诺在考虑对美国海底主导地位的挑战时重申了中华人民共和国中国人民解放军海军（PLAN）作为印度-太平洋地区最大威胁的地位，代表着对抗美国海军的最具创新性的力量之一。然而，在这起事件中，卡瓦诺号更加阐明了中国被视为海底领域主要对手的理由。中国威胁图景的很大一部分源于中国海军将船体下水的速度，8艘093B型（Shang III）型核快速攻击潜艇（SSN）在不到4年的时间里投入使用。 RADM Cavanaugh 还相信美国对中国 SSN 生产的评估，该评估规定中国海军造船厂可以维持类似的生产率至少十年，20-40 艘商 III 或改进型 SSN 可能会在这段时间内投入使用。
卡瓦诺进一步表示，“尚III”级潜艇比以前的中国核潜艇具有重大的质的改进，具有先进的静音技术、24个垂直发射单元库以及推进方法的重大变化。这些改进产生了质的飞跃，以至于“商III”级潜艇可以被认为是一种全新级别的潜艇。 “这表明中国已经准备好进行迭代。他们建造了商，他们建造了商 III，然后他们正在开发下一个产品。我认为迭代本身就有其自身的品质。” ——克里斯·卡瓦诺少将，美国太平洋舰队潜艇部队司令。关于进一步的发展，美国潜艇部队密切关注中国未来的095型核导导弹潜艇的进展，指出其增加的X型舵和泵喷推进装置并不是完全颠覆，而是表明了中国潜艇部队创新和风险吸收的明显趋势。除了095型之外，美国还关注096型和094型弹道导弹核潜艇（SSBN）的发展，这代表着中国核三位一体和二次打击能力的关键发展。也许最关键的是，美国潜艇部队评估了建设和支持日益庞大且质量先进的中国核舰队所需的支持基础设施的持续建设。
卡瓦诺还指出，随着中国在战略和战术层面上不断改进核潜艇的使用，理论方面的改进与配套基础设施和舰队本身的建设相匹配。中国海军研究船东方红3号停靠在青岛。 Cnsphoto 来自路透社。在对解放军潜艇威胁进行评估后，RADM Cavanaugh 进一步强调了解放军为更好地准备其水下部队以应对任何潜在冲突所做的努力，其中海洋学研究、测量和测绘在解放军为应对与美国或其盟国的任何潜在冲突所做的准备中发挥了重要作用。特别是卡瓦

【原文 English Original】
In a series of talks at the Navy Submarine League’s 2026 Annual Symposium, Rear Admiral Chris Cavanaugh (Commander, Submarine Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet – COMSUBPAC) spoke on the state o f adversary developments and activities in the Pacific, highlighting the critical threats facing the U.S. Navy’s submarine fleet. PLAN Submarines The new Type 09IIIB SSN, edited image shared on Chinese social media. RADM Cavanaugh reaffirmed the People’s Republic of China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) position as the top threat in the Indo-Pacific region when considering challenges to America’s undersea dominance, representing the one of most innovative forces facing down the U.S. Navy. However, in this instance, the Cavanaugh shed greater light on the reasoning behind China’s appraisal as the primary adversary in the undersea domain. A large element of China’s threat picture stems from the sheer rate at which the PLAN is able to put hulls in the water, with 8 Type 093B (Shang III) type Nuclear Fast Attack Submarines (SSNs) entering service in under 4 years. RADM Cavanaugh also gave credence to U.S. assessments regarding Chinese SSN production, which stipulate that a similar rate of production is sustainable by PLAN yards for at least a decade, with 20-40 Shang III or improved SSNs potentially reaching service in that timeframe. Cavanaugh further stated that the Shang III represents a serious qualitative improvement over previous Chinese SSNs, featuring advanced quieting techniques, a Vertical Launch Cell bank of 24 cells, and significant changes to the propulsion method. These improvements produced a qualitative jump to such an extent that the Shang IIIs could be considered an entirely new class of submarine. “It points to the idea that China is ready to iterate. They build Shang, they build Shang III, and they’re onto the next thing. And I would argue that iteration itself has a quality on its own.” – Rear Admiral Chris Cavanaugh, Commander, Submarine Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet. In regards to further developments, the U.S. sub force closely monitored processes surrounding the Type 095, China’s prospective nuclear guided missile submarine, pointing to its addition of X-form rudders and pump jet propulsion not as complete upsets, but as demonstrative of a tangible trend of innovation and risk absorption by the Chinese submarine force. Alongside the 095, the U.S. also follows the development of the Type 096 and Type 094 classes of nuclear ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs), representing key developments in China’s nuclear triad and second strike capability. Perhaps most critical, the U.S. sub force assessed the continual buildup of supporting infrastructure needed to build out and support an increasingly large and qualitatively advanced Chinese nuclear fleet. Cavanaugh also noted improvements in doctrine match any build outs of supporting infrastructure and the fleet itself, with the Chinese continually improving in their usage of nuclear submarines at a strategic and tactical level. Other PLAN Activities Chinese Research vessel Dong Fang Hong 3 docked in Qingdao. Cnsphoto via REUTERS. Following his assessment of the PLAN submarine threat, RADM Cavanaugh further highlighted PLAN efforts to better prepare its undersea force for any potential conflict, with oceanographic research, surveying, and mapping playing a large part of this component in PLAN preparations for any potential conflict with the United States or its allies. In particular, Cavanaugh confirmed a Reuters report which detailed Chinese undersea research efforts dedicated in part to mapping key operational areas near the Philippines, Taiwan, Guam, and Hawaii, including ingress and egress routes near large submarine bases in the latter two locations. Whilst these mapping efforts and the Chinese-linked vessels conducting them possess valid scientific rationale for their presence under international law, the Navy assesses this research as a vital step in preparing any undersea battlefield. Combined with increased Chinese investments across the board in Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (UUVs), their support ships, and other submersibles, the Navy assesses the Chinese approach to be more holistic in nature, identifying, laying out, and executing key steps in an organized manner to improve the sub-sea force in all aspects. The U.S. Navy assesses that all of these steps, including mapping efforts, expansion of the Chinese submarine industrial base, and continual iteration coalesce into a methodical approach designed to eventually level the playing field in the undersea domain. Russian Efforts Kazan, the first Russian Project 885M Yasen-M-class SSGN, now under operation by Russia’s Pacific Fleet. Russian MOD picture. After the PLAN, Cavanaugh highlighted Russia as the next key adversary facing America under the Pacific’s waves, presenting a somewhat different threat profile. At the top of the list includes Russia’s continual investment into its at-sea strategic deterrent, presenting mostly in the form of newer Project 955 Borei-class (also known as the Yury Dolgorukiy-class) of SSBNs, with both baseline Project 955 and newer Project 955A standard boats under Russian Pacific Fleet operation. “If you saw a graph of undersea defense threats, they’re growing rapidly. I’m talking about SSGNs, SSBNs, with Russia and China combined. And so that has significant implications for our ability to maintain domain awareness with our own force structure.” – Rear Admiral Chris Cavanaugh, Commander, Submarine Forces, U.S. Pacific Fleet. Cavanaugh also briefly highlighted another leg of Russia’s undersea strategic deterrent in the Poseidon nuclear XLUUV (also known as Status-6) as an unconventional threat profile that the U.S. Pacific submarine force would have to grapple with. Amongst the slides, alluded to was the threat presented by Russia’s Yasen or Severodvinsk-class of SSGNs, presenting an extremely quiet class of boats capable of carrying dozens of hypersonic or cruise missiles within close proximity to the U.S.’s coast. Combined with continued and dedicated Russian undersea efforts, Cavanaugh stressed that Russia’s consolidation of newer sea-based nuclear deterrents and continued investments into its submarine fleet still makes it a potent threat, especially when considered in conjunction with the Chinese fleet. Additionally, even as the Russian surface fleet continues to succumb to aging vessels and budget constraints, the Russian sub force will likely remain an important consideration for the threats facing U.S. undersea dominance. Last but Not Least: North Korea Image of the new North Korean SSBN during an inspection conducted by North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un. Image taken from a North Korean State Media Broadcast. North Korea’s threat profile came at the tail end of Cavanaugh’s remarks on the threats facing the U.S. submarine force and sub-sea efforts. Whilst North Korean advancements were of note, in the eyes of the U.S. Navy and its top brass, the substance backing Pyongyang’s claims remains to be seen. Despite this, any potential North Korean advancements list as increasingly consequential, especially considering the domain of at-sea nuclear capabilities. The recently revealed North Korean SSBN as well as suspected claims of advancement in torpedo and propulsion technology depict the main subjects noted in Cavanaugh’s remarks. Whilst the U.S. Navy currently withholds any final judgements on validity of the claims surrounding North Korean improvement, Cavanaugh noted that these developments represent part of an increasingly dense under-sea threat environment coming from three different countries, each with their own intricacies. title: China Lifts The Veil On Its GJ-11 Mysterious Dragon Stealth UCAV
